title: Finite-type ideal defining the boundary of a quasi-compact open space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space and let $U\subseteq T$ be a quasi-compact open subspace. Then there exists a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ such that $|V(\mathcal K)|=|T|\setminus|U|$ and $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$. Here $V(\mathcal K)$ is the closed subspace defined by this ideal [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], and point sets carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. No Noetherian or reducedness assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 0855 (lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals), implication (2) to (3); the unit restriction follows from the displayed equality of vanishing sets.

proof.text: Put $C=|T|\setminus|U|$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] the open subspace $U$ has $|U|$ identified with an open subset of $|T|$, so $C$ is closed. By [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] choose the reduced closed subspace $Z\hookrightarrow T$ with $|Z|=C$. The ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] gives its quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_T\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$. On $U$ the base-changed closed subspace is empty: its point space is the inverse image of $C$, which is empty. On each scheme test the closed immersion with empty point space has zero structure sheaf, so the quotient description in the correspondence gives $\mathcal J|_U=\mathcal O_U$.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation] to $\mathcal J$ on $T$. The assumed quasi-compact scheme atlas of $T$ has continuous surjective point map by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so $|T|$ is quasi-compact. Absolute quasi-separatedness is the diagonal hypothesis of this item. We obtain a small filtered diagram of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal F_a$ and maps $\phi_a:\mathcal F_a\to\mathcal J$ whose colimit in all module sheaves is $\mathcal J$. We will take the image of a single $\phi_a$, rather than require the approximating modules to embed.

source.place: Tag 0855, finite-type approximation step; Tag 0829 (lemma-directed-colimit-finite-type), proof via Tag 07V9.

proof.text: The assumed quasi-compact scheme atlas of $U$ has a continuous surjective point map by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so $|U|$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] choose a representable surjective etale map $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$. Its composite $W\to T$ is representable etale: on a scheme test $B\to T$, the fibre product $B_U$ is open in $B$, and $W\times_TB\to B$ is the composite of an etale map to $B_U$ with its open inclusion. Both the open-immersion and composition assertions are [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus $W\to T$ is an affine object of the small etale site.

By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], evaluation on $W$ computes the filtered colimit of step 2, giving $\varinjlim_a\mathcal F_a(W)\cong\mathcal J(W)=A$. By the element-representation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], there are an index $a$ and $s\in\mathcal F_a(W)$ with $\phi_a(s)=1\in A$. Hence the image of $\phi_a$ on $W$ is the whole module $A$.

Set $\mathcal K=\operatorname{im}(\mathcal F_a\xrightarrow{\phi_a}\mathcal J\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T)$. Images of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent and computed on affine etale charts by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. On each such chart $V$, $\mathcal F_a(V)$ is finitely presented, hence finitely generated; the images of a finite generating set generate $\mathcal K(V)$. The same chart criterion proves that $\mathcal K$ is of finite type. Its inclusion into $\mathcal O_T$ makes it an ideal, with $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal J$. On $W$ it is the unit ideal by step 4. The quotient $\mathcal O_U/\mathcal K|_U$ therefore restricts to zero on the surjective etale covering $W\to U$; a sheaf locally zero is zero. Consequently $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$.

By the inclusion-reversing ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal J$ implies $Z=V(\mathcal J)\subseteq V(\mathcal K)$, so $C\subseteq|V(\mathcal K)|$. Conversely the restriction of $V(\mathcal K)$ over $U$ is defined by the unit ideal, hence is empty on every scheme test. If a point of $V(\mathcal K)$ mapped into $U$, its field-valued representative would factor through the open subspace $U$ by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], producing a point in that empty fibre product. Thus $|V(\mathcal K)|\cap|U|=\varnothing$, and $|V(\mathcal K)|=C$, as required.
